items.title: Many Mississauga Ward 7 candidates missed the meeting where residents could ask questions
items.summary: Of the 17, only seven candidates attended the meeting to share their priorities and answer public questions. More than 30 people attended the Ward 7 candidates meeting on Sept. 14. Of the 17 candidates vying to be Mississauga’s next Ward 7 representative, seven municipal election hopefuls attended a meeting to share their thoughts on a range of issues affecting the community. The Sept. 14 meeting, organized by the Applewood Heights and Hills Residents’ Association, was held at the Royal Canadian Legion branch on Dundas Street, where more than 30 people turned out to hear from candidates about crime, affordability and e-scooters, among other issues. Here’s what each candidate said, in part, at the meeting. A former manager with Safe City Mississauga who spent a decade in crime prevention and the non-profit sector, Adad said he wants to move beyond election-cycle promises. “I will take problems of today not as something to get your vote on Oct. 26, but as an opportunity to build the solutions of tomorrow,” he said. Alves, a former Peel District School Board trustee, said new housing development in the city was not being built with Ward 7 families in mind.

items.title: Where can Mississauga voters go to cast their ballot in advance of Oct. 26?
items.summary: Advance voting will open on Oct. 6 until Oct. 7 at Mississauga City Centre. Ahead of election day, Mississauga residents can cast their ballots through advance voting, which begins Oct. 6. The city has announced that eligible voters can take advantage of early voting to avoid long lines on election day which is Oct. 26. Oct. 6 to 7: Advance polling begins at Mississauga Civic Centre located at 300 City Centre Dr. for voters across the city. Oct. 8 to 11: Advance polling begins at all 11 citywide ward locations. Residents can cast their votes at any location regardless of which area or ward they live in. This flexibility is only valid for early voting period.

items.title: Mayoral Debate Reveals Rare Consensus on a New Parking Garage for Troubled Ridgeway Plaza
items.summary: According to INsauga, the idea of building a four-storey parking garage behind Ridgeway Plaza came up Friday afternoon during Mississauga's first mayoral debate of the election season, held at Sheridan College's Hazel McCallion Campus. A moderator asked the four main candidates what they would do to make the west-end plaza, home to roughly 115 restaurants, more pedestrian and traffic friendly. Incumbent Carolyn Parrish, who won a mayoral byelection in June 2024 after Bonnie Crombie left for provincial politics, pointed to a large plot of land behind the plaza and said a paid parking facility there would pay for itself within three to four years. INsauga reports that while the four candidates, who also included city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla, disagreed on most issues during the nearly two-hour debate, they largely agreed on building a new parking garage at Ridgeway Plaza. Crombie, who served as Mississauga's mayor from 2014 to 2024 before leaving to lead the Ontario Liberal Party, told the debate audience she is concerned for residents living near the plaza who have dealt with noise and other problems in recent years.

items.title: A Carolyn Parrish surprise and 3 other key takeaways from the Mississauga mayoral debate
items.summary: Incumbent mayor claims she has convinced Premier Doug Ford to change the Peel police funding formula. The Mississauga mayoral debate hosted by CBC and the Mississauga Board of Trade on Friday featured some unexpected claims about the police funding formula. Mississauga Mayor Carolyn Parrish says she has convinced Premier Doug Ford to fix the Peel police funding formula that she argues has left Mississauga residents unfairly paying more than Brampton for years. Parrish made the claim on the stage of the first mayoral debate of the campaign Friday afternoon, after facing criticism for resigning from the Peel police board, a decision she has defended as necessary to challenge unprecedented police budget increase requests. Parrish said she met the premier at his home six weeks ago and that he committed to making the change when the legislature reconvenes in November. ’ And he said ... ‘November, when the house is back in session,’” Parrish told reporters after the debate. ” She said isn’t sure what the exact proposal would be though she’d be happy with a 50-50 split over the current 62-38 that leaves the bulk of the cost on Mississauga taxpayers, she said. Brampton Mayor Patrick Brown has pushed back on the idea that the formula is unfair, citing specific costs that come from Mississauga linked to Pearson airport, for which they get partially reimbursed, and the marine unit. “Mayor Brown doesn’t want to talk about it,” Parrish said Friday. “Would you? He’s had amazing advantage for the last few years.

items.title: Thousands of Salmon Push Upstream Through the Credit River as Mississauga's Annual Run Gets Underway
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, an annual salmon run is now underway in the Credit River, drawing thousands of fish swimming upstream from Lake Ontario in what the city calls an annual phenomenon. The city says the run typically begins each September in Mississauga, as well as in parts of Brampton and Caledon, and continues through the end of October, usually peaking in early October. INsauga reports that some of the best spots in the city to witness the event include Erindale Park, The Riverwood Conservancy's Riverwood Park and Meadowvale Conservation Area. According to the city, the salmon push against the current of the Credit River each late summer and early fall to spawn and lay their eggs. City officials explain that as water temperatures cool and fall rains raise water levels, freshwater salmon begin their yearly trek from the mouth of Lake Ontario up the Credit River to spawn. The city encourages residents of all ages to come witness the natural event for themselves.

items.title: Mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie wants the TTC subway extended to Mississauga’s city centre. But will Doug Ford buy in?
items.summary: Mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie wants to extend Toronto’s Line 2 subway to Mississauga’s city centre. Mississauga mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie is proposing to extend the TTC’s Line 2 subway from Kipling to Mississauga city centre, creating a central transit hub. Mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie says it’s time for an extension of the east-west Bloor-Danforth subway line to Mississauga’s city centre — and if elected she will launch a feasibility study and appeal to a subway-loving premier and a prime minister looking for nation-building projects. “Vaughan has a subway and one is being planned for both Markham and Richmond Hill. ” said Crombie in an interview. ” The Hurontario LRT or Hazel McCallion line, which is currently under construction as a north-south spine that will extend through Mississauga’s city centre into Brampton, made sense at the time of planning more than a decade ago and was the more affordable option, Crombie said. “We didn’t have the density then, but we do have the density today and we have the demand for it,” she said. Carolyn Parrish, who is running for re-election as mayor, has been a fan of the idea of a Mississauga subway for several years, and lamented that McCallion shot the idea down when she was mayor decades ago. But Parrish has also cited the hefty price tag as a barrier, unless the province is willing to pick up the tab of $1 billion per kilometre. “Listen, if somebody is going to put a subway out to Mississauga, there’s no way anybody in their right mind would turn it down with traffic (as it is) now,” Parrish told Insauga last year. Parrish did not respond to a request for comment Thursday.

items.title: City Weighs a Second 'Signature Park' Just North of Kariya Park in Mississauga's Downtown Core
items.summary: According to INsauga, the City of Mississauga is exploring plans for what staff describe as a possible second signature park in the city's downtown core, just steps north of the existing Kariya Park. City staff wrote in a report going to council on Tuesday that the new greenspace could become a distinctive and memorable public space and a focal point for residents and visitors in the Downtown Core. The proposed site sits at the corner of Burnhamthorpe Road West and Kariya Drive, though at just under one acre it would be significantly smaller than Kariya Park itself. Raj Sheth, the city's commissioner of community services, said in the report that the new park's proximity to Kariya Park, already regarded as one of the city's most treasured public spaces, offers a chance to complement and enhance the broader park experience in that part of downtown. Staff are recommending the city enter into a memorandum of understanding with developer Camrost Felcor to explore an enhanced park design for the city-owned property at that southwest corner, according to INsauga. The greenspace under consideration sits adjacent to a site Camrost Felcor is currently developing.

items.title: Weekly Yard Waste Pickup Returns This Fall as Peel Region Preps a Bigger Service Handoff to Brampton
items.summary: According to INsauga, weekly yard waste pickup is set to begin again this fall across Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon, with residents able to check their own collection calendar or sign up for free reminders to find their pickup day. Acceptable yard waste includes leaves, yard rakings with debris, tree trimmings and branches, brush and hedge clippings, household and garden plants, and Halloween pumpkins without the candle, INsauga reports. The outlet notes grass clippings are not accepted either at the curb or at Community Recycling Centres, and all yard waste at the curb must go in kraft paper bags or reusable containers clearly marked as yard waste, since plastic bags are not accepted. Looking further ahead, INsauga reports that starting in October of next year, the City of Brampton will take over garbage, organics and yard waste collection for both Brampton and Caledon, a service currently handled by the Region of Peel. According to INsauga, that shift is part of a broader provincial restructuring of services across Peel Region that is moving several responsibilities from the regional government to Brampton, Caledon and Mississauga.

items.title: Attempted Murder Charge Upgraded to Second-Degree Murder After Labour Day Stabbing Victim Dies
items.summary: According to INsauga, a Mississauga woman now faces a second-degree murder charge after the victim of a Labour Day weekend stabbing died in hospital four days after the attack. Peel Regional Police say officers responded to a stabbing in the area of Dixie Road and Dundas Street East in the city's east end and found a man with a serious stab wound to the neck, who was taken to hospital in critical condition. INsauga reports the stabbing happened outside a shelter on Dundas Street near Main Street, several blocks east of Dixie Road. The day after the attack, police arrested and charged 42-year-old Lorena Sanchez of Mississauga with attempted murder, and she was held in custody pending a bail hearing, according to police. After the victim died, homicide investigators took over the case, and police say Sanchez's charge was upgraded to second-degree murder when she appeared again in Brampton court on September 18. Peel police are asking anyone with information about the incident to contact the Homicide and Missing Persons Bureau.

items.title: UPDATE: Victim Succumbs to Injuries following a Stabbing in Mississauga
items.summary: Region of Peel – Investigators from the Homicide and Missing Persons Bureau have upgraded the charges against a woman in connection with a stabbing in Mississauga. On Sunday, Sept. , officers responded to reports of a stabbing that occurred in the area of Dixie Road and Dundas Street East. Upon arrival, officers located an adult male suffering from a serious stab wound. He was transported to hospital in critical condition. The following day, 42-year-old Lorena Sanchez of Mississauga was arrested and charged with Attempted Murder. She was held in custody pending a bail hearing at the Ontario Court of Justice in Brampton. On Sept. 10, the victim succumbed to his injuries and the Homicide and Missing Persons Bureau took the carriage of this investigation. On Sept. 18, Sanchez was brought to the Ontario Court of Justice in Brampton where her charges were upgraded to Second Degree Murder. Anyone with information regarding this incident is asked to contact investigators with the Homicide and Missing Persons Bureau at 905-453–2121, ext. 3205. ca Phone: 905-453-2121, ext.
